Respondent __________________________________________ Issued and entered This 8th day of July 2024 by Jeffrey Hayden Special Deputy Director ORDER I. PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND On June 6, 2024, authorized representative for (Petitioner), filed with the Director of the Department of Insurance and Financial Services a request for an external review under the Patient’s Right to Independent Review Act, MCL 550.1901 et seq. The request for review concerns the denial of prior authorization for surgery. The Petitioner receives health care benefits through Meridian Health Plan of Michigan, Inc. (Meridian), a health maintenance organization. Ambetter from Meridian is the plan administrator. The benefits are described in Meridian’s 2023 Evidence of Coverage Ambetter Core (the EOC). The Director notified Meridian of the external review request and asked for the information used to make its final adverse determination. Meridian responded on June 6, 2024. The Director accepted the request for external review on June 13, 2024. The Director assigned an independent review organization to analyze the medical issues in this appeal. The review organization submitted its report to the Director on June 26, 2024. II. FACTUAL BACKGROUND The Petitioner had hammertoe and right foot pain with history of type II diabetes. The Petitioner failed treatment with orthotics, toe spacers, debridement of the lesions on the foot, injections, and oral medications. On May 16, 2024, Dr. diagnosed the Petitioner with curly toes 4th and 5th and DM II. On October 17, 2022, the Petitioner had a percutaneous flexor tenotomy, an orthopedic procedure to File No. 226146-001 Page 2 increase blood flow through small cuts in the tendon to promote healing performed by Dr. Following surgery, the Petitioner still complained of pain so Dr. recommended the Petitioner seek a second opinion. On September 28, 2023, the Petitioner was seen for a second opinion with Dr. who recommended correction via proximal interphalangeal joint fusion and arthroplasty and requested prior authorization from Meridian. Meridian denied the request on the basis its medical policy criteria were not met; therefore, the surgery is not medically necessary. The Petitioner appealed Meridian’s decision through its internal grievance process. At the conclusion of that process, Meridian issued a final adverse determination dated April 1, 2024, affirming its coverage denial. The Petitioner now seeks the Director’s review of that determination. III. ANALYSIS Petitioner’s Argument In the request for external review, the Petitioner’s authorized representative wrote: On behalf of the aforementioned patient, … please accept this request for an external review for the surgical repair of multiple deformities of his right foot. On page two of form FIS 0018, I have provided a brief chronological summary of the care the patient has received for his foot since establishing care at our office, STEM Health Systems, in February 2022. Attached you will find detailed office visits, podiatry consults, operative and imaging reports, additional pre-operative planning, and insurance letters. I have also included articles written by podiatrists that explain hammer and curly toe deformities, treatment options, and expected outcomes. [The Petitioner] has several years long history of foot and ankle problems, including foot drop surgery and gout in his ankles. While I cannot be certain of the cause of [the Petitioner’s] deformities, some possibilities are wearing ill-fitting shoes, nerve damage, and diabetes. Prior to establishing care with us on February 1, 2022, he was evaluated in the emergency room for elevated glucose levels, and subsequently diagnosed with Type II Diabetes Mellitus. His problems precede this new diagnosis, but diabetes potentially contributed to worsening of the condition. Research states that hammer and curly toe deformities can be treated with physical therapy and orthotics in the early stages. This patient has been suffering with this condition for years, and previous physical therapy, home exercise programs, spacers, and taping have failed. We referred him to a podiatrist, and on October 17, 2022, Dr. completed a Percutaneous Tenotomy of the patient's 4th and 5th toes of the right foot. This procedure was unsuccessful, and the patient complained of increased and additional pains. Dr. discussed additional procedure options, including File No. 226146-001 Page 3 bone resection and small joint fusion, but ultimately recommended the patient pursue a second opinion. We then referred [the Petitioner] to Dr. , DPM. Dr. evaluated the patient, noted additional findings, planned for surgical repair (\"arthrodesis 4th toe right foot PIPJ with pin fixation, arthroplasty 5th toe derotational with temporary pin fixation and excision of exostosis right 5th toe\") but was denied by the patient's insurance company, stating they did not receive documentation of why the surgery was needed. [The Petitioner’s] attempted to appeal this decision himself, without the assistance of medical professionals, and likely without the medical records the insurance company initially requested. On April 1, 2024, Ambetter from Meridian sent [the Petitioner] a final denial letter, stating \"this service is not considered medically necessary for your condition,\" and \"there is no documentation that you had received a period of conservative care including pain medication, padding, debridement of lesions, steroid injections, or orthotics before surgical intervention was planned.\" It is my professional opinion that surgical intervention is the only option; physical therapy and orthotics are no longer indicated after a failed surgical repair, worsening pain, further deformity, and rigidity. [The Petitioner] has failed pain medications, bracing, and home exercise programs all in the last two years. The increase in pain has caused [the Petitioner] to compensate by walking on the inside of his foot, which can lead to more discomfort. He is a self-employed laborer, specializing in laying flooring. He has been unable to work for some time, as his job requires him to stand, kneel, and squat for prolonged periods of time. Due to the circumstances, the patient consented to and completed a PHQ-9 in office recently, with a score of 21, and started on antidepressants for situational depression. On behalf of [the Petitioner], I am requesting he be approved to receive the previously planned surgical repair by Dr. , DPM. Please review the attached documentation at your earliest convenience. Thank you for your time and understanding in this matter. I look forward to hearing from you. Respondent’s Argument In its final adverse determination, Meridian wrote: Ambetter from Meridian has reviewed your appeal received on 03/06/2024 regarding surgery on your toe. We have upheld our decision based on the following rationale: We cannot approve your request for a procedure to correct a deformity of the second, third or fourth toes (Correction Hammertoe) at this time. Based on the approval criteria for your plan InterQual 2023, Mar. 2023 Release CP: Procedures Arthrodesis or Arthroplasty, Interphalangeal Joint, Second-Fifth Toes, this service is not considered medically necessary for your condition a deformity of the second, third or fourth toes in which the main toe joint is bent upward like a claw (Hammertoe). This is because there is no documentation that you had received a period of conservative care including pain medication, File No. 226146-001 Page 4 padding, debridement of lesions, steroid injections, or orthotics before surgical intervention was planned. Please speak with your provider about alternative treatment options. Director’s Review The Director assigned an independent review organization (IRO) to evaluate Meridian’s criteria and help determine whether the surgery to correct a deformity of the second, third, or fourth toes (Correction Hammertoe) is medically necessary for treating the Petitioner’s condition. This review is required by section 11(7) of the Patient's Right to Independent Review Act, MCL 550.1911(7). The IRO reviewer is a physician who is board-certified in podiatric medicine and is in active practice. The IRO reviewer’s report included the following analysis and recommendation: Are the plan’s criteria for Hammertoe Correction surgery, InterQual 2023, Mar. 2023 Release CP: Procedures Arthrodesis or Arthroplasty, Interphalangeal Joint, Second-Fifth Toes, consistent with the standard of care? Please explain. The criteria are consistent with the standard of care. The criteria require the deformity to be evident on clinical and radiographic examination with continued symptoms secondary to the deformity despite conservative treatment. If they are, does the member meet these criteria? Please explain. The member meets criteria as the hammertoe deformities are causing pain that interferes with daily activities. The deformities as described on physical examination, and as evidenced by radiographs, meet the components specified in the guidelines. The deformities have continued to cause pain despite the use of accommodative shoes, padding, debridement’s, injections, and orthoses. The IRO reviewer recommended that the Director reverse Meridian’s denial of coverage. The Director is not required to accept the IRO’s recommendation. Ross v Blue Care Network of Michigan, 480 Mich 153 (2008). However, the recommendation is afforded deference by the Director. In a decision to uphold or reverse an adverse determination, the Director must cite “the principal reason or reasons why the director did not follow the assigned independent review organization’s recommendation.” MCL 550.1911(18)(b). The IRO’s review is based on extensive experience, expertise, and professional judgment. In addition, the IRO’s recommendation is not contrary to any provision of the Petitioner’s certificate of coverage. MCL 550.1911(17). The Director, discerning no reason why the IRO’s recommendation should be rejected in the present case, finds that surgery to correct a deformity of the second, third or fourth toes (Correction Hammertoe) is medically necessary, and therefore, is, covered under the Petitioner’s benefit plan. File No. 226146-001 Page 5 IV. ORDER The Director reverses Meridian Health Plan of Michigan, Inc.’s April 11, 2024, final adverse determination. Meridian shall immediately provide coverage for the requested surgery to correct a deformity of the second, third or fourth toes. See MCL 550.1911(19). Further, Meridian shall, within seven days of providing coverage, furnish the Director with proof it has implemented this order. To enforce this order, the Petitioner may report any complaint regarding its implementation to the Department of Insurance and Financial Services, Office of Appeals, Legal Research, and Market Regulation, at this toll-free telephone number: (877) 999-6442. This is a final decision of an administrative agency. Under MCL 550.1915, any person aggrieved by this order may seek judicial review no later than 60 days from the date of this order in the circuit court for the Michigan county where the covered person resides or in the circuit court of Ingham County. A copy of the petition for judicial review should be sent to the Department of Insurance and Financial Services, Office of Appeals, Legal Research, and Market Regulation, Post Office Box 30220, Lansing, MI 48909-7720. Anita G. Fox Director For the Director: ____________________________________ Jeffrey Hayden Special Deputy Director ", "text_truncated": false}

Respondent __________________________________________ Issued and entered this 6th day of May 2024 by Jeffrey Hayden Special Deputy Director ORDER I. PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND On April 9, 2024, authorized representative of (Petitioner), filed with the Director of the Department of Insurance and Financial Services a request for an external review under the Patient’s Right to Independent Review Act, MCL 550.1901 et seq. The request for review concerns the denial of coverage for outpatient mental health services. The Petitioner receives health care benefits through Meridian Health Plan of Michigan, Inc. (Meridian). The benefits are described in Ambetter from Meridian’s (Ambetter’s) 2023 Evidence of Coverage Ambetter Core (the EOC). The benefits are administered by an entity named “Ambetter from Meridian”. The Director notified Meridian of the external review request and asked for the information used to make its final adverse determination. Meridian responded on April 17, 2024. The Director accepted the request for external review on April 18, 2024. The issue in this external review can be decided by a contractual analysis. The Director reviews contractual issues pursuant to MCL 550.1911(8). This matter does not involve medical issues requiring analysis by an independent review organization. II. FACTUAL BACKGROUND On December 28, 2023, the Petitioner received neuropsychological testing from KaraLee & Associates, PC (KaraLee), an in-network specialist provider. The amount charged was $1,735.00. Meridian denied coverage on the basis that prior authorization was required but not obtained. Meridian notes the File No. 224557-001 Page 2 Petitioner has a $0.00 obligation for the services. The Petitioner appealed Meridian’s decision through its internal grievance process. At the conclusion of that process, Meridian issued a final adverse determination dated April 12, 2024, affirming its coverage denial. The Petitioner now seeks the Director’s review of that determination. III. ANALYSIS Respondent’s Argument In its final adverse determination, Meridian wrote: Ambetter from Meridian has reviewed your grievance received on 4/9/2024 concerning the denial of claim and have determined that the claim was denied because the provider did not request prior authorization. Contracted providers cannot bill members for services that are not authorized. The provider can submit a claim reconsideration. Petitioner’s Argument In the request for external review, it was noted: … Unfortunately, we do not have any updates or new information for you. We have been getting nothing but the run around from Meridian Ambetter. Every time that we call, they push the timeline out and state a different / lengthier amount of time than they originally did in regards to the appeal process. At this point we are not hopeful that they will grant the appeal or rectify their customer service department’s error in giving us the incorrect benefit information (not notifying us that the testing required a preauthorization) prior to the testing being performed. Meridian Ambetter has still not ‘officially’ responded (meaning responded in writing as promised and legally required) regarding our appeal and as of today state that the claim is ‘still under review’ and will not give a new ETA on completion / resolution. We understand that this situation is very frustrating. KaraLee followed all guidelines and protocols for verifying the benefits and required authorization prior to services being performed. Meridian Ambetter concurs and is apologetic for the misinformation, but they don’t seem to consider this worthy of claim payment at this time and as with most insurance companies, likely have a clause written into their policy to protect them from situations like this such as: “Verification of eligibility and/or benefit information is not a guarantee of payment.” At this point, KaraLee is out the full cost of the testing and the generation of the testing results (which as you are aware have not been released due to nonpayment) and in addition we have also spent much time and company / employee resources in continuously following up and attempting to right this situation to no avail. Meridian File No. 224557-001 Page 3 Ambetter has also requested four chart audits on [The Petitioner’s] records since January (all of which were handled promptly on our side). We are assuming that they are doing this based on our appeal request made regarding the testing, however, regardless of their reasoning these requests are also quite time consuming as well and have still yielded no response or resolution from Meridian Ambetter. We cannot continue utilizing multiple members of our staff’s valuable time and resources attempting to pursue / follow up on this on a routine basis having rendered no payment for the services performed and given that this situation was caused due to no fault of our own whilst Meridian Ambetter honors none of their promises made regarding timelines or us receiving things in writing. At this point in time, we would highly recommend that you file a formal complaint and grievance with Meridian Ambetter regarding their employees giving out misinformation pertaining to benefits thus causing your daughter’s claim to deny and remain denied / unpaid months after the fact (given their inability to process our appeal in a timely manner). Every insurance company has a protocol for this and perhaps you will have better luck than we have in getting resolution from them. All the information that would be required from our side can be obtained in the original email I sent you (representative names and reference numbers for the initial calls made prior to testing). As previously stated, if your primary concern is receiving the testing results, you may pay Private Pay to receive the information. If Meridian Ambetter ever pays, you will be promptly reimbursed. We will follow up with you if and when we receive a formal response from Meridian Ambetter regarding this issue. Director’s Review Under “Prior Authorization” (page 38)1 in the certificate, it states: Prior Authorization Required Some medical and behavioral health covered service expenses require prior authorization. In general, network providers must obtain authorization from us prior to providing a service or supply to a member. However, there are some network eligible expenses for which you must obtain the prior authorization. *** Failure to Obtain Prior Authorization Failure to comply with the prior authorization requirements will result in benefits being reduced. 1 This same language is on page 1 of the EOC under Guaranteed Renewable. File No. 224557-001 Page 4 Network providers cannot bill you for services for which they fail to obtain prior authorization as required. The Schedule of Benefits states: The Schedule of Benefits is a summary of services that may be covered under this plan. Benefits listed are subject to all provisions and limitations as outlined in the Evidence of Coverage (EOC). Please reference the EOC for details regarding the benefits listed below. … For services that require prior authorization, network providers must obtain authorization from us prior to providing a service or supply to a member. In addition, the Schedule of Benefits, states that for mental/behavioral health outpatient services, prior authorization is not required for PCP or Other Practitioner visits. The EOC (page 62) states: Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Benefits The coverage described below is designed to comply with requirements under the Paul Wellstone-Pete Domenici Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act of 2008. If you need mental health or substance use disorder treatment, you may choose any provider participating in our behavioral health and substance use disorder provider network and do not need a referral from your PCP in order to initiate treatment. The EOC defines network provider (page 23) as: … any licensed person or entity that has entered into a contract with Ambetter Meridian to provide covered services to members enrolled under this policy including but not limited to, hospitals, specialty hospitals, Urgent Care facilities, physicians, pharmacies, laboratories and other health professionals within our service area. On December 28, 2023, the Petitioner received mental health outpatient services at KaraLee. The amount charged was $1,735.00. In this case, Meridian said prior authorization was not obtained and there is no documentation indicating that prior authorization was requested. However, Meridian supplied phone records indicating that KaraLee called on December 11, 2023, prior to the date of service, to verify benefits. Within the records from Meridian, it shows that the provider inquired about four specific procedure codes (procedure codes 96137, 96136, 96133, and 96132), which are the same procedure codes that were billed for the December 28, 2023, date of service. Further, the records show that for the procedure codes the provider called Meridian about, the provider was told neither a referral nor authorization is required. File No. 224557-001 Page 5 Therefore, since the records from Meridian state that prior authorization is not required for the services the provider billed for the December 28, 2023, date of service, the Director finds that Meridian’s coverage denial was inconsistent with the terms of the Petitioner’s benefit plan. IV. ORDER The Director reverses Meridian Health Plan of Michigan’s April 12, 2024, final adverse determination. Meridian shall immediately process the December 28, 2023, claim. See MCL 550.1911(19). Meridian shall, within seven days of providing coverage, submit to the Director proof it has implemented this order.
